theorem_title: Strict improvement of the preprocessing saving
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSumSharpTail.sharp_saving_strict (c θ : ℝ) (hc : 10 < c)
    (hθ0 : 0 < θ) (hθ9 : θ < 9 / 10) :
    0 < ThreeSumSharpTail.oldSaving c θ ∧
    ThreeSumSharpTail.oldSaving c θ < ThreeSumSharpTail.sharpSaving c θ := by sorry
natural_language_statement: For every real $c>10$ and $0<\theta<0.9$, $$\gamma_*(c,\theta)>\gamma(c,\theta)>0.$$ This compares preprocessing savings at the same parameters. It does not by itself establish a smaller 3SUM running-time exponent.

readback.readback: For every pair of real numbers $c,\theta$ satisfying $c>10$ and $0<\theta<9/10$, let $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm extended to be $0$ at zero and to equal the logarithm of the absolute value at negative arguments. Then both strict inequalities $0<\theta\log((c-1)/9)/\log4$ and $\theta\log((c-1)/9)/\log4<[cH(1/c)-cH((1-\theta)/c)-\theta\log9]/\log4$ hold. Here $c$ ranges over real numbers, not only integers; the arguments of the logarithms appearing after expansion of $H$ are positive under these hypotheses. None of the boundary values $c=10$, $\theta=0$, or $\theta=9/10$ is included.
